inspiration.observed_pattern: A recursive parent-child walk feeds one grouped JSON_OBJECTAGG map for the deepest reachable node.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reduced to one root, one child, and one grandchild while retaining recursive expansion, maximum-depth grouping, and one-member JSON_OBJECTAGG output.

fixture_notes: Root 901 reaches Leaf at maximum depth 2. The single grouped JSON object contains only Leaf and its selected depth, isolating recursive maximum-depth selection from object-member ordering.
determinism_notes: Node IDs, parent links, names, recursive depth, maximum-depth selection, and final ordering are fixed. No clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent schedules are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE mini_org_nodes (node_id INT PRIMARY KEY, parent_id INT NULL, node_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, FOREIGN KEY (parent_id) REFERENCES mini_org_nodes(node_id))

steps.sql: WITH RECURSIVE hierarchy (root_id, node_id, node_name, depth) AS (SELECT node_id, node_id, node_name, 0 FROM mini_org_nodes WHERE parent_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT h.root_id, n.node_id, n.node_name, h.depth + 1 FROM hierarchy AS h INNER JOIN mini_org_nodes AS n ON n.parent_id = h.node_id), deepest AS (SELECT root_id, MAX(depth) AS max_depth FROM hierarchy GROUP BY root_id) SELECT h.root_id, JSON_OBJECTAGG(h.node_name, h.depth) AS depth_map FROM hierarchy AS h INNER JOIN deepest AS d ON d.root_id = h.root_id AND d.max_depth = h.depth GROUP BY h.root_id ORDER BY h.root_id

checks.sql: SELECT node_id, parent_id, node_name FROM mini_org_nodes ORDER BY node_id
